title: Stacked kinematics, x, v and a against t: how are position, velocity and acceleration linked?
summary: Three panels share one time axis: position on top, velocity in the middle, acceleration at the bottom. Each lower panel is the slope of the one above, so features line up vertically and the chain of derivatives can be read by eye.

media.alt: Three stacked line plots over time 0 to 6: a teal sine wave for position x, an amber cosine wave for velocity v and a blue negative sine wave for acceleration a, with a shared time axis at the bottom.
media.caption: Reference render of class F4.4 (design-system gallery). The data are synthetic and exist only to demonstrate the form.

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data. Standard theory only.

read_the_figure.question: How are position, velocity and acceleration linked?
read_the_figure.axes: Shared horizontal axis: time t from 0 to 6 (no units given). Top: x, -1 to 1. Middle: v, -1 to 1. Bottom: a, -1 to 1. The panels have separate vertical axes and no units.
look_at: When x is at its maximum, what is v and what is a?
When v is at its maximum, where is x?
How is a related to x in shape and sign?
Which panel's slope is the panel below it?
as_drawn: The curves are x = sin t, v = cos t and a = -sin t, so a = -x: simple harmonic motion with angular frequency 1.
x is at its maximum near t = 1.57 where v = 0 and a = -1; v is at its maximum at t = 0 where x crosses zero going up and a = 0.
All three panels span -1 to 1 because for unit frequency and amplitude the amplitudes of x, v and a are equal; for other values they would differ by factors of omega.
read_the_figure.proves: That the three curves are consistent derivatives of each other at the level of shape and timing. It cannot prove the numbers: no units are shown.
if_wrong: Panels with different time ranges: the vertical alignment lies.
Velocity computed by differencing noisy position data without smoothing: the middle panel is noise.
No units on y axes: sizes cannot be compared.

terms.meaning: A quantity and its first and second time derivatives.
The rate of change of a curve; the value of its derivative.
Motion with acceleration proportional to minus the displacement, giving a sinusoid.
A time offset between waves of the same frequency; v leads x by a quarter period.
Panels aligned so equal t lines up vertically.
A point where the slope is zero: where v = 0 for x, a = 0 for v.

remember: v = dx/dt: the slope of the top panel; a = dv/dt: the slope of the middle panel.
Peaks of x line up with zeros of v; peaks of v with zeros of a.
For SHM, a = -omega^2 x: acceleration is x flipped and scaled.
Shared t axis, separate y axes, labelled units.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Three lines share a horizontal axis and have separate vertical ones. The colour is only a label for the quantity. Position along the horizontal axis is time, so vertical guide lines connect the same instant across all three.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: Position, velocity and acceleration are one thing seen at three levels of differentiation. Stacked on a shared time axis, the slope of the top panel can be compared with the height of the middle panel and the slope of the middle with the height of the bottom. The relationship becomes a visual rule: where one is zero, the next derivative's panel has an extreme.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: Separate vertical scales make the sizes comparable only if the units are given; here they are not. The eye compares slopes poorly when the panel aspect ratios differ. A differentiated noisy signal amplifies noise. And the three panels equal in amplitude is a coincidence of unit frequency, not a rule.

understand.title: Why each required item matters
understand.text: A shared time axis is the whole reason to stack the panels. This render shows it and nothing else is on the list. Adding units and a vertical guide line at a chosen instant would make the reading precise.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: A phase plot of v against x shows the same motion as a closed curve (F4.7) with no time axis. For an energy view see F4.5. For noisy data integrate acceleration to get v and x, which is stable, rather than differentiating position.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Add a vertical cursor at t = 1.57 across all panels with the values written in, and label the units (m, m/s, m/s^2).

steps.title: The chain of derivatives
steps.tex: x=\sin t\ \Rightarrow\ v=\dot x=\cos t\ \Rightarrow\ a=\dot v=-\sin t=-x
steps.note: A finite-difference check on 6001 points gives v within 2e-7 of cos t and a within 3e-7 of -x. The curves in the figure are consistent derivatives.

steps.title: The conserved quantity
steps.note: Energy conservation of the oscillator: when |x| is large, |v| is small, and the reverse.

worked.title: Reading the reference render
worked.problem: From the figure: (1) at the first maximum of x, what are v and a? (2) Where is v largest? (3) How does a compare with x?

solution.text: The first maximum of x is at t = 1.57. There v = 0 and a = -1, the most negative value.
At t = 0 (and t = pi, 2 pi ...), where x crosses zero: v = 1 at t = 0.
a is x turned upside down: a = -x at every t.

worked.answer: At the top of x the velocity is zero and the acceleration is most negative; v peaks where x crosses zero; a = -x.

checks.q: At a peak of x, what is v?
checks.answer: Zero: the slope of x is zero at a peak.

checks.q: x = 3 sin(2t). What is the amplitude of a?
The v panel is almost the same shape as the x panel shifted a quarter period. What kind of motion is this?
checks.answer: Sinusoidal (simple harmonic) motion: v = x shifted by pi/2 and scaled by omega.
